questions.qtext:
In a system, there are n resource, R1, R2, ..... Rn, each protected by a binary semaphore S1, S2, ..... Sn respectively.
There are large number of processes and each process can request one or more resource at a time.
Each process must request resources in the order: R1 → R2 → R3 ..... Rn
A process will request resource using P(Si) for each resource and then release with V(Si).
Which of the following statements is correct for this system?

options.text: Deadlock can still occur because mutual exclusion and hold-wait condition remain.
Deadlock is possible due to violation of the no-preemption rule.
Deadlock is still possible if multiple process requests all n resources simultaneously.
Deadlock is prevented because the circular wait condition is avoided.

questions.solution:
(d)
The rule (R1 → R2 → R3) breaks circular wait condition.

questions.qtext:
A process generates the following page reference string 7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4, 2, 3, 0, 3
Assume the system used 3 frames and all frames are initially empty. The page replacement
algorithms considered are Optimal (OPT), Least Recently Used (LRU) and First-in_First-out (FIFO).
Which of the following statements are incorrect?

options.text: LRU and optimal replacement algorithm result in the same number of page faults.
FIFO result in less page faults than LRU.
Increasing the number of frames from 3 to 4 leads Belady’s anomaly in FIFO.

questions.solution:
(d)
(a) Optimal has 7 page faults.
LRU has 9 page faults.
(b) FIFO has 10 page faults more than LRU.
(c) Increasing frames, increases page fault in FIFO.

questions.qtext:
Which of the following tasks is/are the responsibility of the Memory Management Unit (MMU):
T1 : Translating a virtual address to a physical address using both the outer and inner page tables.
T2 : Allocating memory for the inner page table when a new page is accessed for the first time.
T3 : Raising a page fault of a required virtual page is not present in the inner page table.
T4 : Updating the outer page table when a new page table is allocated for a new memory segment.
questions.solution:
(c)
• The MMU does not allocate memory, it only uses page tables for translation.
• The MMU does not modify page tables, it only reads, them.
The OS updates the outer page table when a new segment/page table is created.

questions.qtext: Consider a 2-level paging hardware with TLB. Assume that the entire page table and all the pages are in the physical memory. It takes 50 μs to search the TLB and 40 milliseconds to access the physical memory. If the TLB hit ratio is 0.6 and there are no page faults, the effective memory access time (in milliseconds) is ________.
questions.subject: Technical

options.text: In demand paging, a given instruction can lead to page faults.
Demand paging brings a page into the memory only when it is needed.
Demand paging requires more main memory than normal paging.
Demand paging may bring entire process into memory at load time (for very smaller processes).

questions.solution:
(a, b, d)
• The process of loading the page into memory on demand (whenever page fault occurs) is known as demand paging.
• Lazy swapper concept is implemented in demand paging in which a page is not swapped into the memory unless it is required. So option (b) is correct.
• Option (c) is false because a process larger than the main memory can be executed because of
demand paging. The OS itself loads pages of a process in main memory as required.
• More processes may be maintained in the main memory: Because we are going to load only
some of the pages of any particular process, there is room for more processes. This leads to
more efficient utilization of the processor because it is more likely that at least one of the
more numerous processes will be in the ready state at any particular time.

questions.qtext:
A surveillance system stores video recordings of unknown length, written sequentially. File grow over time and random access is rarely needed. Metadata overhead should be minimum.
Which file allocation method is most suitable?

options.text: Contiguous allocation, due to minimal metadata and optimal access time.
Linked allocation, as it allows dynamic growth with low overhead.
Indexed allocation, for scalability and block level direct access.
Contiguous allocation, since fragmentation is avoided and access is predictable.

questions.solution:
(b)
Linked allocation allows sequential access, dynamic growth and low metadata overhead.
